units.passage: Members of the Tufts community have a duty to uphold integrity and professional standards, ensuring they use AI responsibly and for mutual benefit. Tufts’ commitment to academic freedom means that responsible AI use will, and should, look different across disciplines, roles, and contexts. Community members hold diverse views about AI, from embracing it as essential preparation for students’ futures to viewing it as contrary to educational values and goals. Standards will continue to evolve as we further develop our understanding of AI tools and their capabilities, limitations, and impacts. Any AI use must remain consistent with Tufts’ fundamental values and existing policies on academic integrity and professional conduct, as outlined in school handbooks and relevant policies. This mutual trust is foundational to our community: students, faculty, and staff depend on each other to use AI in ways that support learning, teaching, clinical care, administrative work, and scholarship, and they should recognize that AI choices affect both individual work and our shared academic endeavor. 4. units.passage: If you use generative AI, make sure to disclose your use of AI.
units.policy: Students who use generative AI make sure to disclose their use of AI.
units.why: 'make sure to disclose your use of AI' instructs students to acknowledge AI use; the imperative gives a should-level modality given the guide's advisory tone ('As you make decisions'). Type P24 (disclose with submission).

units.passage: This might look like citing it as a source, describing how you used it in the Methods section of your paper, or something else! It's crucial that you are transparent about how you're using AI
units.why: 'It's crucial that you are transparent about how you're using AI' strengthens the disclosure rule by asking for transparency about how AI was used; it stays with P24 since no tool or prompt detail (P25) is required.
units.fit_note: Asks for transparency about how AI was used; examples (citing as a source, describing in Methods) are loose, not a prescribed format, and no required form or tool/prompt details (not P25).

units.passage: Being transparent about when and how you use AI tools, such as ChatGPT, can help maintain trust and clarity in academic work.
units.why: 'Being transparent about when and how you use AI tools, such as ChatGPT, can help maintain trust and clarity in academic work' recommends disclosure. P24 fits, and the wording is advisory ('can help'), so the modality is should.
units.fit_note: Advisory; no required statement or format.

units.passage: When AI is involved in your work (whether writing, coding, analysis, or planning), it is helpful to let others know.
units.why: 'it is helpful to let others know' when AI is involved in writing, coding, analysis or planning extends disclosure to all kinds of work, including code. P24 fits and the advice is non-binding, so should.
units.fit_note: Advisory, covers coding and analysis as well as writing; no format.

units.passage: Where and how should students disclose their use of AI?
units.why: 'Where and how should students disclose their use of AI?' is a prompt for instructors to decide a disclosure rule. P24 fits.
units.fit_note: A question to consider, not a rule.

units.passage: To adhere to our scholarly values, students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work (this includes in-text citations and/or use of quotations, and in your reference list).
units.why: The same sample says 'students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work', which is a citation rule. P24 fits.
units.fit_note: Sample statement from UMass Amherst offered as a model.

units.passage: I reserve the right to ask you if or how you used AI in a specific assignment or activity.
units.why: 'I reserve the right to ask you if or how you used AI in a specific assignment or activity' lets the instructor ask about use. P24 is nearest because it asks for disclosure when requested.
units.fit_note: Coder A (P24): Disclosure on request rather than with every submission. Coder B (P34): Asking about AI use, not explaining the work itself.

units.passage: If you utilize ChatGPT for any part of the assignment (from idea generation to text creation to text editing), you must properly cite ChatGPT.
units.why: 'you must properly cite ChatGPT' applies to any part from 'idea generation to text creation to text editing'. P24 fits.

units.passage: Even when it is allowed, there may be limits or expectations including how to
units.why: 'Even when it is allowed, there may be limits or expectations including how to give credit to GenAI' warns that allowed use may still carry conditions. P24 fits partly.
units.fit_note: Coder A (P24): Also says allowed use may come with other limits. Coder B (P24): Only says credit may be expected; no rule of its own.

units.passage: Acknowledging and citing the use of AI increases transparency and builds trust.
units.why: 'Acknowledging and citing the use of AI increases transparency and builds trust' gives the reason for disclosure. P24 fits.

units.passage: Acknowledgement or disclosure statements address when and how you have used AI tools and could be provided in an appendix or a cover letter.
units.why: 'Acknowledgement or disclosure statements address when and how you have used AI tools and could be provided in an appendix or a cover letter' describes a disclosure statement. P24 fits.
units.fit_note: Format guidance (appendix or cover letter) rather than a mandate.

units.passage: Citation is needed when you are directly referencing or incorporating an AI output in your text.
units.why: 'Citation is needed when you are directly referencing or incorporating an AI output in your text' says when citation is required. P24 fits.

units.passage: Professional associations that offer citation style guidelines for GenAIinclude:
units.why: 'Professional associations that offer citation style guidelines for GenAI include: American Psychological Association (APA)... MLA ... Chicago' lists citation formats. P24 fits partly.
units.fit_note: Coder A (P24): Lists style guides to use; does not itself require the tool, prompt or date (P25). Coder B (P25): Points to style guides but does not say what to include.

units.passage: Be transparent about the use of AI. Disclose when a work product was created wholly or partially using an AI tool and, if appropriate, how AI was used to create the work product. Non-disclosure could be considered misrepresentation or plagiarism if the AI generated content is presented as human work.
units.why: "Be transparent about the use of AI. Disclose when a work product was created wholly or partially using an AI tool" is a plain imperative to disclose AI use, so P24, must; AI use stays allowed as long as it is disclosed.

units.passage: Be transparent about the use of AI. Disclose when a work product was created wholly or partially using an AI tool and, if appropriate, how AI was used to create the work product. Non-disclosure could be considered misrepresentation or plagiarism if the AI generated content is presented as human work.
units.why: Adds "if appropriate, how AI was used to create the work product", a request to describe how AI was used; P24 nearest since it names no tool, prompt or output.
units.fit_note: Asks for a description of how AI was used, conditional on appropriateness, not specific citation details.

units.passage: Any AI-assisted content should be properly attributed, and users should consult the University’s Intellectual Property Policy and Copyright Infringement and Illegal File Sharing Policy before incorporating AI-generated materials into their work.
units.why: "Any AI-assisted content should be properly attributed", a citation duty, P24, should.

units.passage: Any AI-generated media used for research, education, or creative projects should be clearly labeled as synthetic content to prevent misinformation or deception
units.why: AI media used for "research, education, or creative projects should be clearly labeled as synthetic content," a labeling duty; closest is P24 disclosure.
units.fit_note: Requires labeling AI-generated media as synthetic to prevent deception, not disclosure of AI assistance on submitted work. / Labeling of synthetic media to prevent misinformation, rather than acknowledging AI help in a submission.

units.passage: They should disclose if AI was used to assist in the creation of official documents and formal reports
units.why: Employees "should disclose if AI was used to assist in the creation of official documents," workplace disclosure, P24.

units.passage: This includes using the assistance of A.I. text generators to perform central requirements of an assignment (i.e., reading, synthesizing, interpreting, writing, coding, programming, etc.) without both the explicit permission of the instructor and complete attribution and citation of A.I.-assisted components.
units.why: The same sentence requires "complete attribution and citation of A.I.-assisted components" when AI is used; a citation duty, P24.

units.passage: The following are examples (not exhaustive) of sources that require citation or acknowledgment: written text in any format, including Powerpoint slides or other presentation modality; blog posts or any commentary found on social media platforms; podcasts and video lectures; articles found in journals and periodicals, whether print or online; someone else’s published statements, ideas, data, or illustrations; work that appears on websites, whether authored by named individuals, institutionally authored, machine authored, or listed as anonymous; ideas, summaries, drafts, data, code, and text generated via A.I.
units.why: Sources requiring citation include "ideas, summaries, drafts, data, code, and text generated via A.I."; AI output must be cited, P24.

units.passage: Consider requiring them to comprehensively explain how they used AI tools as part of the assignment (see “When do I need to acknowledge that I have used a Gen-AI tool in my coursework?” in the FAQs for students below).
units.policy: Instructors should consider requiring students to comprehensively explain how they used AI tools as part of the assignment.
units.why: "Consider requiring them to comprehensively explain how they used AI tools as part of the assignment" is advice that instructors ask for disclosure. P24 fits; the actor is the instructor.

units.passage: cite a generative AI tool whenever you paraphrase, quote, or incorporate into your own work any content (whether text, image, data, or other) that was created by it
units.policy: Cite a generative AI tool whenever you paraphrase, quote, or incorporate into your own work any content (text, image, data, or other) that it created (MLA, quoted).
units.why: The MLA quote says "cite a generative AI tool whenever you paraphrase, quote, or incorporate into your own work any content". That is a duty to cite AI-created content, P24.

units.passage: acknowledge all functional uses of the tool (like editing your prose or translating words) in a note, your text, or another suitable location
units.policy: Acknowledge all functional uses of the tool, such as editing prose or translating words, in a note, your text, or another suitable location (MLA, quoted).
units.why: "acknowledge all functional uses of the tool (like editing your prose or translating words)" extends disclosure to functional uses, P24.

units.passage: You should also acknowledge other functional uses of these tools, including but not limited to generating ideas for an assignment and identifying potential sources for research.
units.policy: Students should also acknowledge other functional uses of AI tools, including generating ideas for an assignment and identifying potential sources for research.
units.why: "You should also acknowledge other functional uses... generating ideas for an assignment and identifying potential sources for research." Disclosure of idea and source use, P24.

units.passage: When in doubt, acknowledge your use of the tool.
units.why: "When in doubt, acknowledge your use of the tool." A when-unsure default to disclose, which is not a type exactly; P24 is nearest.
units.fit_note: Says to disclose when unsure, a default toward disclosure.

units.passage: The most important thing is that you make clear exactly how you used the tool.
units.why: "The most important thing is that you make clear exactly how you used the tool." Core disclosure principle, P24.

units.passage: Kim Acquaviva, UVA nursing faculty member and Faculty AI Guide, asks her students to complete this transparency statement with every major assignment as a way to hear from the students how they're using generative AI.
units.policy: Students complete an AI transparency statement with every major assignment.
units.why: "asks her students to complete this transparency statement with every major assignment" requires disclosure with each submission, P24.

units.passage: Cite AI tools using your class’s citation style (APA, MLA, etc.)
units.why: The tip 'Cite AI tools using your class’s citation style (APA, MLA, etc.)' directs students to cite AI use in their work, giving no detail of prompt or output, so P24 rather than P25.

units.passage: You must properly acknowledge when and how AI tools have been used in your submissions.
units.why: Template 1 states 'You must properly acknowledge when and how AI tools have been used in your submissions': disclosure with each submission (P24).

units.passage: When AI use is permitted, students must disclose how AI was used through appropriate citations.
units.why: 'Students must disclose how AI was used through appropriate citations' when AI is allowed: disclosure/citation of AI use (P24).

units.passage: The policy would benefit from clear attribution requirements for AI-created visual content that maintain transparency and accountability.
units.why: The Visual Media Policy needs 'clear attribution requirements for AI-created visual content' (P24, nearest).
units.fit_note: An attribution rule for institutional visual media, not student submissions; also deepfakes (P75).

units.passage: Guidelines emphasize human oversight, fact- checking, and disclosing AI use in coursework.
units.why: 'disclosing AI use in coursework' is named as part of the guidelines (P24).

units.passage: Disclosing GenAI use is often advisable and may be mandatory ; failure to do so may have serious consequences, particularly in published research or coursework
units.why: 'Disclosing GenAI use is often advisable and may be mandatory' addresses disclosure, noting failure may have serious consequences in coursework, so P24 (not P28, since it states no safe-harbor rule).

units.passage: Here is an example of how I would like you to disclose your use of AI: [insert example here].
units.why: The template asks instructors to give 'an example of how I would like you to disclose your use of AI': communicating disclosure expectations, P24.

units.passage: Citation expectations for AI-generated content
units.policy: Faculty should clearly state citation expectations for AI-generated content.
units.why: Faculty should state 'Citation expectations for AI-generated content'; this leaves the citation rule to the instructor, so it is partly P24 (disclosure) but sets no citation requirement itself.
units.fit_note: Instructors are told to state citation expectations; the page does not itself require students to disclose or cite AI. / Instructors decide whether and how to cite; the university requires no disclosure.

units.passage: How may students most effectively demonstrate that their work – whether in draft or final form – is either entirely their own or properly cited? (“You may incorporate AI-generated content or ideas in assignments, but you must cite this content, and you must fact-check all material, because AI-generated content often contains falsehoods and fictional sources. Citations must include which AI platform generated the content, and the specific prompts used to generate content
units.why: The sample says 'You may incorporate AI-generated content or ideas in assignments, but you must cite this content', which allows AI with citation, P24.

units.passage: Ideas and content generated by you, and those that are AI-generated, should be clearly delineated and cited accordingly.
units.why: The second sample says 'Ideas and content generated by you, and those that are AI-generated, should be clearly delineated and cited accordingly', a disclosure rule, P24.

units.passage: Transparency in students’ AI usage (i.e. being forthright about when and how AI tools were used in completing assignments or projects)
units.why: The integrity discussion lists '(1) Transparency in students' AI usage' (being forthright about when and how AI was used), a disclosure expectation, P24.

units.passage: Proper acknowledgment by students of AI assistance (similar to citing a source), when AI tools have contributed to idea generation, writing, problem -solving, or other academic tasks
units.why: '(2) Proper acknowledgment by students of AI assistance (similar to citing a source)' is an acknowledgment rule, P24.

units.passage: W&M should establish rules for appropriate GenAI use, including restrictions on inputting sensitive data and requirements to disclose GenAI-generated content
units.why: 'requirements to disclose GenAI-generated content' is the second usage rule W&M should establish, P24.
units.fit_note: Stated as a rule W&M should establish, with no detail on form.

units.passage: You must clearly indicate in yo ur citations when and how you used AI for brainstorming purposes. It is an honor code offense to use AI tools for more than brainstorming without explicit permission. CATEGORY 4 - AI for Limited or Specific Tasks You may use AI tools as outlined by your instructor in the assignment guidelines.
units.why: 'You must clearly indicate in your citations when and how you used AI for brainstorming purposes' is disclosure with each submission (P24); student, during-work, must.

units.passage: You must clearly indicate in your citations when and how you used AI for these purposes
units.why: 'You must clearly indicate in your citations when and how you used AI for these purposes' (P24); student, during-work, must.

units.passage: Communicate when and how GenAI is used as appropriate for discipline and context.
units.why: 'Communicate when and how GenAI is used as appropriate for discipline and context' is a learning goal about disclosing AI use (P24); student, general, informs.

units.passage: Acknowledgement of AI Use: Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT 4o, Claude, and Copilot were used as thought partners and writing collaborators throughout the planning and writing of this document
units.why: 'Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT 4o, Claude, and Copilot were used as thought partners and writing collaborators' discloses AI use in writing the appendix, P24.
units.fit_note: A disclosure by the report's authors, not an instruction to others.

units.passage: If you plan to allow it, consider when/how/in what way AI-generated content should be cited and whether to require students to turn in, or at least retain, AI chat transcripts
units.why: 'consider when/how/in what way AI-generated content should be cited' asks instructors who allow AI to set citation rules (P24).
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors as a design consideration, not a student requirement.

units.passage: If applicable, provide information on how students are expected to cite Generative AI use for assignments. See the UWM Library resource on using and citing Generative AI
units.why: "provide information on how students are expected to cite Generative AI use" tells instructors to supply citation instructions; closest is P24 though the rule is the instructor duty to explain citation.
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors: supply citation expectations, not the student duty itself. | Directs instructors to explain citation expectations; the disclosure rule itself binds students.

units.passage: Furthermore, you must cite Generative AI when it is used.
units.why: "you must cite Generative AI when it is used" is a disclosure duty with each submission, P24.

units.passage: All assignments that use any external source must be credited using a proper citation.
units.why: "All assignments that use any external source must be credited using a proper citation" requires crediting sources, P24 (with AI a covered source).

units.passage: Students are permitted to use advanced automated artificial intelligence or machine learning tools on assignments in this course if instructor permission is obtained in advance. Unless given permission to use those tools, each student is expected to complete each assignment without substantive assistance from others, including automated tools. Option 3: Use only with acknowledgement Students are permitted to use advanced automated artificial intelligence or machine learning tools on assignments in this course if that use is properly documented and credited.
units.why: Option 3 lets students use the tools "if that use is properly documented and credited", so AI use is conditional on attribution; P24 (disclose AI use with each submission).
